summary: Defines the Cache-Status HTTP response header field, a standard way for caches to explain how they handled a request. Before this, caches added ad hoc headers for this. The field aligns with HTTP's caching model and helps with debugging. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Each storage shelf stamps a note saying whether it had your item or had to fetch it.

questions: how to tell if a response came from cache
what is the cache-status ttl parameter
subtitle: A standard HTTP header that lets each cache report how it handled a request.

tldr.problem: HTTP caches often add their own header fields to explain how they handled a request, but the meaning and syntax differ between implementations.
tldr.mechanism: The Cache-Status response header is a Structured Fields List with one member per cache, each carrying parameters such as hit, fwd, fwd-status, ttl, stored, collapsed, key and detail.
tldr.outcome: People and tools can read one consistent description of every cache in the chain, though the RFC warns that the information can help attackers probe caches.

today: RFC 9211 is a Proposed Standard. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
To aid debugging, by humans and automated tools, HTTP caches often append header fields to a response explaining how they handled the request. Unfortunately the semantics of these fields are often unclear, and both semantics and syntax vary between implementations.

RFC 9211 defines one new HTTP response header field, Cache-Status, with standardized syntax and semantics. It uses terminology from HTTP Semantics (RFC 9110) and HTTP Caching (RFC 9111).
sections.eli5: Every cache used to leave notes in its own handwriting. This RFC says everyone should use the same form.

sections.title: The Cache-Status Field
sections.content:
The syntax conforms to Structured Field Values (RFC 8941). The value is a List, and each member stands for a cache that handled the request. The first member is the cache closest to the origin server, and the last is the one closest to the user, possibly the user agent's own cache.

Each member identifies its cache with a String or Token, which could be a product or service name, a hostname, an IP address or a generated string. Parameters on each member are OPTIONAL, though caches are encouraged to provide as much information as possible.

Caches decide when to add the field: some always, others only when configured or when a request activates a debugging mode. An intermediary SHOULD NOT add a member to a response it generated locally, such as a 400 for a malformed request, unless the response is based on a stored response, as with 304 or 206. When adding a value, caches SHOULD preserve the existing field value so the whole chain can be debugged.
sections.eli5: As a package moves from the warehouse to your door, each stop adds a line to the list, so the list reads in order of the trip.

sections.title: The Parameters
sections.content:
The RFC defines eight parameters:

  • hit: a Boolean that is true when the cache satisfied the request without forwarding it. A stale response used without going forward, for example because the origin is unavailable, can count as a hit. hit and fwd are exclusive.
  • fwd: a Token saying why the request went toward the origin. The values are bypass, method, uri-miss, vary-miss, miss, request, stale and partial. The most specific reason known SHOULD be used.
  • fwd-status: an Integer with the status code the next hop returned. It is meaningful only with fwd, and defaults to the status code sent in the response.
  • ttl: an Integer with the remaining freshness lifetime in seconds, as calculated by the cache. It may be negative to show staleness.
  • stored: a Boolean saying whether the cache stored the response. Meaningful only with fwd.
  • collapsed: a Boolean saying whether the request was collapsed with other forward requests. Meaningful only with fwd.
  • key: a String conveying a representation of the cache key, which may be implementation specific.
  • detail: a String or Token for extra information. Its meaning is always specific to the cache that sent it, and it is intentionally limited.
sections.eli5: The note can say 'I had it', or 'I had to ask the warehouse, and here is why', plus how fresh the item is and whether I kept a copy.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives a minimal hit, Cache-Status: ExampleCache; hit, and a more informative one with ttl=376. A stale hit shows negative freshness, such as ttl=-412. A complete miss is fwd=uri-miss, and a miss that validated on the backend is fwd=stale; fwd-status=304.

For several layers, members appear in order from the origin outward. In the three-layer example, a reverse proxy served from cache, a forward proxy forwarded with uri-miss, collapsed the request and stored the result, and the browser cache forwarded with uri-miss.
sections.eli5: Reading the notes from top to bottom tells you the story: the first shelf had it, the next had to ask, and the last had nothing.

sections.title: New Parameters and IANA
sections.content:
New parameters are registered in the "HTTP Cache-Status" registry, which IANA created and filled with the parameters above. Requests are reviewed by a designated expert; a specification document is appreciated but not required. The expert should weigh community feedback, whether the value is well defined, and a preference for generic over vendor-specific parameters. A request gives a name, a Structured Type, a description and optionally a reference.

IANA also added Cache-Status to the HTTP Field Name Registry as a permanent entry referencing RFC 9211.
sections.eli5: If someone needs a new kind of note, they can ask a referee to add it to the official list.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Attackers can use Cache-Status to probe the behavior of the cache and other components and to infer the activity of those using the cache. The field may not create these risks by itself, but it can help in exploiting them. For example, knowing whether a cache stored a response can help in a timing attack on sensitive data, and exposing the cache key can help in cache poisoning attacks.

Merely obfuscating the key does not mitigate the risk. The field can be omitted, sent only to authorized clients, or sent with sensitive parts such as key only to authorized clients.
sections.eli5: The notes show how the shelves work, which could help a sneaky person, so show them only to people you trust.

viz.caption: THE fwd REASONS, MOST SPECIFIC TO LEAST (RFC 9211)

items.label: Bypass
items.desc: The cache was configured to not handle this request.

items.label: URI miss
items.desc: No stored response matched the request URI.

items.label: Vary miss
items.desc: URI matched, but no response could be selected using Vary.

items.label: Miss
items.desc: No usable response; used when uri-miss and vary-miss cannot be told apart.

items.label: Request
items.desc: A fresh response was found, but the request did not allow its use.

items.label: Stale
items.desc: A response was selected but it was stale.

items.label: Partial
items.desc: Only a partial response was found.
